title: The Factory That Dreams: 39 AI Agents, No Framework - Rushabh Doshi, Machinecraft
talk_summary: A 100-person thermoforming factory owner built a 36-agent go-to-market system with no fine-tuning, using off-the-shelf models over a layered memory (vectors + graph) with a nightly consolidation 'dream cycle' and a corrections-wins rule. The transferable core is memory architecture and specialist-agent separation, not the biology metaphor or the marketing.

takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated agent guards human corrections so that when a human fixes something, the correction overrides conflicting stored facts permanently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Memnon, my favorite, guards corrections. So, the second a human fixes something, it stays fixed forever.

takeaways.what_they_do: A gate decides what is worth remembering so the store does not fill with junk, plus layered memory (working, pinned facts, episodes, relationships).
takeaways.evidence_quote: A salience gate that decides what's even worth remembering, so the brain doesn't fill up with junk.

takeaways.what_they_do: A scheduled offline pass replays the day, consolidates useful facts, hunts contradictions, forgets stale items, and promotes repeated work into reusable skills, producing a report.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every night, Eira runs a sleep cycle. It replays the day, locks in useful stuff, hunts for contradictions

takeaways.technique: One agent, one job + specialist debate
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one mega-prompt, each specialist has exactly one job, and a coordinator pulls specialists in to argue until a single answer emerges.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one prompt that's supposed to do everything ends up doing everything badly... One agent, one job. It's a team, not a hero.

takeaways.technique: Cross-check before speaking, cite source and date
takeaways.what_they_do: Guardrail rules require cross-checking multiple sources and citing the document and date rather than asserting absolutely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: No single source has the whole truth. So, cross-check before you speak. Never say things absolutely. Cite the document and the date.

takeaways.technique: No fine-tuning, retrieval over off-the-shelf models
takeaways.what_they_do: They skipped training entirely, chunked private history into vectors plus a relationship graph and let stock models extract facts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We never trained a model. No GPUs humming in the basement, no fine-tuning.
takeaways.numbers: built for ~$30k vs $230k agency quote; runs on a couple thousand dollars a month
